guarantees.claim: encode_bytepad gets the combinatorial result of sha3_pkg::encode_bytepad_len(strength_i) every cycle.

assumptions.claim: Input strength_i must be a legal strength enumeration value accepted by sha3_pkg::encode_bytepad_len.
assumptions.risk: An illegal strength_i could cause an undefined or corrupted encode_bytepad, breaking the bytepad length and ultimately the KMAC security strength.

formal.consequent: strength_i inside {128, 256} // typical KMAC strengths, actual set from package

formal_sketch.consequent: strength_i inside {128, 256} // typical KMAC strengths, actual set from package

uncertain_points.claim: Comment states that for a 128‑bit secret key only the lower 16 bits of encode_keylen are valid. It is unclear whether the upper bits are guaranteed to be zeroed or if they can contain undriven/uninitialized values, which could leak secret‑dependent state when the encoded key is assembled.
uncertain_points.risk: If upper bits are not explicitly cleared or masked before concatenation, internal junk bits may enter the security‑critical key encoding stream, violating zeroization or secrecy assumptions.

security_implications: encode_keylen is used for secret key length encoding. If upper bits are not properly masked when a shorter key is used, hardware could inadvertently expose internal state or secret length. Additionally, strength_i directly influences the bytepad length and therefore the effective security strength of the KMAC operation; an unchecked illegal value could weaken the algorithm.
